dominant_breach: long-duration trusts can preserve private control and transfer-tax planning across generations while ordinary claimants and public revenue systems see only fragmented or delayed ownership signals
fastest_washout: perpetual or multi-century duration, GST allocation, trust migration, directed-trust control, and decanting/mutation wash out intergenerational circulation before enforcement can observe the control chain

trust_duration_perpetuity_risk.note: Fail when governing law allows long-duration control without equivalent beneficiary or public visibility.

dynasty_trust_gst_lock_in.note: Watch/fail until GST allocation and transfer-tax incidence are connected to wealth-tier evidence.

dynasty_trust_rule_against_perpetuities.note: Watch because duration depends on state law and asset class; no one-size perpetuity claim may pass.

directed_trust_control_separation.note: Fail when trustee title is separated from protector/advisor/investment/distribution control without a control-party map.

trust_decanting_and_migration_risk.note: Watch/fail where migration or decanting can reset visibility, remedy, or governing-law assumptions.

trust_beneficial_ownership_visibility.note: Fail unless legal-arrangement control parties and ultimate effective controllers are identifiable to relevant claimants or authorities.
